finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filePath with a malicious value that includes shell metacharacters, leading to command execution.
finding.assumptions: The filePath is derived from user input or an untrusted source.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is std::ifstream::open which simply passes the file path to the OS file-opening API; it does not invoke a shell or execute a command. No exec-family functions are called, and no system() or similar wrappers are present. Thus shell metacharacters in filePath cannot lead to command execution.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a query with a malicious value that includes shell metacharacters, leading to command execution.
finding.assumptions: The query is derived from user input or an untrusted source.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the code for any system or exec family calls (system(), exec*, popen, etc.) that would use the regex query as a command. None are present. The regex is constructed purely for in‑memory pattern matching, not passed to a shell. Therefore no OS command injection path exists.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide values for filePath, lineNumber, and offset that include shell metacharacters, leading to command execution.
finding.assumptions: The filePath, lineNumber, and offset are derived from user input or an untrusted source.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Verified that the code does not perform any OS command execution; the string built at line 36 is only used as part of a Result data structure and never passed to a system call or shell invocation. No exec, system, or similar functions are present, and there is no path from the constructed string to a command interface.
